A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BAT/CGP research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across the expanded appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original baseline reproductions, BAT component ablations, downstream benchmark results, and layer-wise representation analyses in Sections 4–6 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains original experiments and adds detection, bird classification, speech recognition, smaller-model results, and measured computational costs in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Equation (7) changes the stated local regression loss normalization from all N tokens to the masked-token count |Im|. BAT's principal components and CGP's aggregation/prototype procedure remain intact. The PDFs establish a revision to the written objective, without establishing whether the implementation changed.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates AudioSet, ESC-50, and Speech Commands classification. v2 retains these and adds BirdSet HSN bird classification under distribution shift, DCASE2016 Task 2 sound event detection, and LibriSpeech speech transcription, substantially extending domains and task requirements.

E2.justification: v2 adds BEATs as an evaluated backbone alongside EAT and SSLAM. Table 5 also evaluates VQT and Head2Toe, previously discussed without experimental comparisons, and adds linear convex gated probing. ProtoBin, previously compared on EAT/SSLAM in Table 1, now participates in the main BAT benchmark comparison.

E3.justification: v2 explicitly refines final-benchmark settings. Comparing v1 Table 6 with v2 Table 7, AS-2M finetuning changes from 400k to 200k steps, AudioSet probing uses asymmetric BCE, and ESC-50 changes from CE to BCE. The reported AS-2M training count also changes from 1,932,574 to 1,912,024. New temporal-task protocols and ViT-Small evaluation further expand the experimental design; these disclosures do not establish that every retained experiment was rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds an explicit distribution-shift evaluation on HSN and a comparative analysis of probe latency, memory, parameters, and computation in Appendix D. Appendix F expands layer-weight analysis from v1's two classification datasets to six datasets and four backbones. The original frontend, target-selection, and decoder ablations remain.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates. v2 introduces ± values for ESC-50 performance in Table 5 and latency in Table 10. Their statistical meaning and run or seed counts are unspecified, so the PDFs support newly reported uncertainty but not an inferred increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 retain their numerical results, but Table 5 changes extensively under revised settings: BAT's AS-2M CGP mAP is 42.90 in v1 and 45.03 in v2. The reported ESC-50 finding also reverses: CGP exceeds finetuning in v1 but trails it in v2. These are not controlled same-setting gains or losses. Tables 6, 9, and 10 add ASR, BAT-S, and computational results.

T1.justification: Equation (7) replaces division by N with division by |Im|, mathematically changing the local-loss definition because only masked tokens enter the sum. The remaining formal development is essentially retained; neither version introduces theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the central claims that CGP improves frozen representation evaluation, that its guidance produces a stronger BAT audio SSL model, and that standardized implementations improve reproducibility. The abstract and conclusion preserve these claims; v2's broader experiments and expanded explanations strengthen their supporting context.

C2.justification: Section 6 replaces v1's emphasis on anticipated benefits from further hyperparameter tuning with a more specific attribution of AS-2M reproduction gaps to training sampling. v2 also adds substantive qualifications concerning non-prototype probes' dependence on layer normalization, Head2Toe's Lasso/convergence sensitivity, and VQT's inability to train on cached features.

D1.justification: v1 promises code upon acceptance or request; v2 reports an open-source release and supplies a repository address covering BAT and baseline evaluation. It also expands configuration documentation, clarifies attention-gate persistence, and specifies the timing environment, including PyTorch 2.8.0, CUDA 12.8, and an RTX A6000. These substantially improve documented implementation and access information.

R1.justification: The positioning relative to D2V2, EAT/SSLAM, and prototype probing is retained. v2 adds references for DCASE, LibriSpeech, asymmetric loss, and additional bioacoustics work, while removing the BEANS future-work citation. Numerous other reference edits update bibliographic metadata for already discussed work.

P1.justification: The seven main sections retain their order and most methodological exposition. v2 edits terminology and tense, corrects 'CGB' to 'CGP', revises the contribution list and conclusion, reorganizes the appendices, and adds author-contribution and acknowledgement text. These refine the existing narrative without replacing its overall structure.

P2.justification: Table 5 is substantially redesigned around probing methods, backbones, and multiple metrics. Figure 1 clarifies the pooling diagram, and Figure 6 changes from two line-chart panels to a 24-panel layer-weight display. New ASR, smaller-model, and computational-cost tables, together with expanded configuration tables, substantially alter the presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the paper's broad claims through direct comparisons with additional probing methods and BEATs, evaluations beyond classification, and measured computational costs. Expanded implementation information and reported code availability also improve assessability. Undefined ± statistics, conflicting pretraining warmup descriptions, and an overbroad claim that CGP beats all probes despite the ESC-50 exception remain weaknesses. Nevertheless, the added experimental scrutiny addresses important limitations of v1's evidential coverage.
